newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS - HEINEKEN FLAT, FIZZ SEEN RETURNING.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - HEINEKEN FLAT, FIZZ SEEN RETURNING.

text.p: Heineken NV , Europe's biggest brewer, announced a 1.4 percent dip in 1996 year net profits on Friday but said it expected these to pick up again this year.
Net profit fell to 655 million guilders from a previous 664 million, giving net per share of 13.06 guilders versus 13.24 guilders per share.
Trading profit was little changed at around 1.01 billion guilders, while turnover, boosted by recent acquisitions, grew by 20 percent to 12.19 billion guilders from 10.14 billion.
Heineken maintained its dividend at 3.50 guilders per share.
The results were towards the better end of analysts' forecasts which had been for net of 630-660 million guilders.
"A profit growth is expected for 1997. The amount of the profit growth cannot be predicted at the present moment," the company said in a statement.
Heineken said beer markets in Europe and North America would be "virtually stable" this year, while consumption in Asia and South America would show continued, albeit decreasing, growth.

Both the premium beer sector and sales of low-priced beers would become more important in these stable European markets, it said, adding that competition was becoming intense due to changes in distribution, a shift from the hotel, restaurant and cafe trade to the off-premise sector, the concentration in the retail trade and the internationalisation of the beer industry.
All this was pressuring margins on standard beers, it said.

Opting to give only a guarded outlook, Heineken said it should benefit from a further rise in exports and lower raw material and packaging prices, but would remain vulnerable to a range of external factors -- currency moves, excise duties, political unrest, economic developments and the weather.

Heineken said that the world beer market grew by 1.4 percent in 1996, while total sales of beer brewed under its supervision rose by 10 percent to 70.7 million hectolitres and sales of Heineken branded beers rose 4.6 percent to 17.9 million hectolitres.
Heineken's Amstel brand maintained its sales volume of 6.9 million hectolitres in a declining segment market, while its Murphy's stout brand showed significant growth.
Heineken said its exports were a "particularly positive feature", growing by 10 percent in 1996.
Beer consumption was down in most parts of Europe, hit by moderate weather and weaker economies, but these lower sales were offset by gains in sales volumes in America and Asia.
In early Amsterdam trading, Heineken shares leaped around five percent on the results before easing back to stand 2.70 guilders higher at 332.20 guilders each at 0910 GMT.
Analysts gave the figures a broad welcome.

"The figures are towards the upper range of expectations. The outlook is interesting. Heineken is cautious and it looks as if it is trying to temper expectations somewhat," said Darrell Duthie at MeesPierson.

"The results were a little better than expected," another analyst said. "They were a little bit cautious with the prospects, but that was expected, too." -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040
